title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents automation for publisher-type access and User access, which the briefing reports as undocumented. Its caveat about Work IQ MCP policy also overlooks documentation that places connector operations within the policy-governed tool surface.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans federated connectors for governed Work IQ access to additional enterprise data sources.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap products are Microsoft Graph and Work IQ.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Graph", "Work IQ"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Developer platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Developer"]

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for this Work IQ federated-connectors capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ federated connectors default enable participation APIs admin control. Read roadmap, Work IQ overview, federated connectors overview and manage-federated-connectors; existing connector defaults are documented, but no arrival default for this roadmap change is stated.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol to fetch external data in real time.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors access data using the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Administrators manage federated connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Learn describes connected enterprise sources as participating in Work IQ Copilot, entity and schema tools.
claims.quote: Connected enterprise sources participate in Work IQ Copilot, entity, and schema tools. Connected enterprise sources refer to data sources connected in Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs.
claims.quote: Connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs.

claims.claim: The source system enforces permissions for federated connector access.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not copy source data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: External connector data is retrieved into conversational responses.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector provides tools, Copilot can create, update or delete data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval.

claims.claim: New write-capable connector tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: Federated connectors remain read-only in the Researcher agent.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: The general connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, unlike the feature overview's write-action documentation.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: An MCP server firewall may need Microsoft 365 Copilot static egress IP addresses allow-listed.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Federated Copilot connector users need a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools have connector-specific licensing requirements.
claims.quote: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools | Connector licensing | Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites. A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.

claims.claim: Work IQ API cost is variable with usage.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage and can be managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Connector availability and staging are managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector > Enable / Disable / Staged rollout.
claims.quote:
Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections | Turns an individual connector on or pauses it without removing configuration.
Staged rollout | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout

claims.where: controls[0..2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 admin-center allow/block controls for Copilot Connectors also apply through Work IQ APIs.
claims.quote: Existing administrator controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center to allow or block Copilot Connectors also apply when Connectors are accessed through Work IQ APIs.

claims.claim: Tenant Work IQ MCP policy is managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools.
In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls: MCP policy applicability
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that Work IQ MCP policy applies to federated connector operations.
claims.quote:
A separate tenant policy layer evaluates each tool request and blocks mutation operations by default.
For connected data sources, connector paths use call_function for reads and do_action for writes, rather than fetch, create_entity, update_entity, or delete_entity.
claims.fix: Remove 'Microsoft has not confirmed it applies to federated connectors' from controls[3].note and its rendered note, and remove 'Microsoft has not confirmed that the Work IQ MCP policy applies to federated connector operations.' from the prose. The existing description 'General Work IQ MCP control' can remain. The tool reference https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/tool-reference explicitly includes connector operations and says each tool request is policy-evaluated; this does not assert that every other Copilot connector experience uses that policy.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP Policy tab is shown when available.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: An automation operation for the tenant Work IQ MCP policy toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ policy PATCH; Work IQ MCP policy API settings update. Opened policy-governance-mcp, MCP overview and tool reference; searched Graph references. Found UI steps and generic setting semantics, but no operation for this toggle.

claims.claim: No separate tenant control specific to federated connectors in Work IQ is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ federated connectors default enable participation APIs admin control. Read Work IQ overview, manage-federated-connectors, policy-governance-mcp and MCP overview; they document inherited connector controls and general MCP policy, not a separate connector-specific Work IQ tenant switch.

claims.where: Governance controls: no automation for staged rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no automation for federated connector staged rollout as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors staged rollout automation Microsoft Graph API; "federated connectors" "staged rollout" "API". Opened manage-federated-connectors, set-up-custom-federated-connectors and Package Management overview; found UI staging, not its automation.

claims.claim: In Copilot Chat, Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to individual write tools, not the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector. Users can decide which tools to allow.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview supports auditing federated connector actions.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: A definitive list of connectors available to Work IQ at this feature's launch is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ federated connectors default enable participation APIs admin control. Read Work IQ overview and federated-connectors-overview; the gallery list covers Copilot connectors generally, while Work IQ participation requires developer enablement and has no launch-specific list.

claims.claim: Availability for this Work IQ federated-connectors feature beyond the roadmap's Worldwide cloud remains open.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated connectors" availability GCC cloud. Read roadmap, Work IQ overview and custom connector FAQ. Results about Business Applications in Work IQ concern a different capability; no additional-cloud commitment for this feature was found.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review connector permissions, but no controls-table row describes a connector permission control.
claims.quote: Review connector permissions after publisher changes. | The table covers connector availability, publisher-type access, User access, general Work IQ MCP policy and a missing Work IQ-specific switch, not connector tool permissions.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Review connector permissions after publisher changes.' It asks the reader to review a permission control that has no controls-table row; do not add a new row as part of this correction.
